#010

Button does not have a discernible accessible name

button-name  •  UF-00010
Critical axe Controls WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value Level A Axe automated finding
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Users of assistive technology may encounter a button without knowing its purpose.

Location

DOM selector: .margin_top_10.col-md-4.margin_bottom_10:nth-child(2) > .bg_white_custom.padding-bottom-10.sako > iframe .ytmVideoInfoChannelAvatar | Ownership: third_party_embed | Actionability: third_party_controlled

Affected HTML 

<button class="ytmVideoInfoLink ytmVideoInfoChannelAvatar"><img class="ytCoreImageHost ytmVideoInfoChannelLogo ytCoreImageFillParentHeight ytCoreImageFillParentWidth ytCoreImageContentModeScaleAspectFill" alt="thumbnail-image" style="background-color: transparent;"></button>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have inner text that is visible to screen readers
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute
  Element does not have an implicit (wrapped) <label>
  Element does not have an explicit <label>
  Element's default semantics were not overridden with role="none" or role="presentation"

axe description

Ensure buttons have discernible text

Recommended change

Provide meaningful visible button text or an appropriate accessible name such as aria-label when the control is icon-only.

Suggested code pattern 

<button aria-label="Describe button action" class="ytmVideoInfoLink ytmVideoInfoChannelAvatar"><img alt="thumbnail-image" class="ytCoreImageHost ytmVideoInfoChannelLogo ytCoreImageFillParentHeight ytCoreImageFillParentWidth ytCoreImageContentModeScaleAspectFill" style="background-color: transparent;"/></button>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Verify the computed accessible name after the change.

#014

Text color contrast requires review

color-contrast  •  UF-00014
High axe Color contrast WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) Level AA Axe automated finding
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Insufficient contrast between text and its background can make content difficult to read for users with low vision or color-vision deficiencies.

Location

DOM selector: .bg_blue_1 > .size-20.white | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<span class="white size-20">United Nations(UN)</span>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element has insufficient color contrast of 3 (foreground color: #ffffff, background color: #5599dd, font size: 15.0pt (20px), font weight: normal). Expected contrast ratio of 4.5:1

axe description

Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

Recommended change

Check the computed foreground and background colors of the affected text. Normal-sized text should generally have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, while qualifying large text should generally have a ratio of at least 3:1.

Manual review

Required: Yes

axe returned this finding as incomplete when contrast could not be conclusively evaluated automatically. Background images, gradients, transparency, overlapping elements, or other rendered styling can require manual inspection.

Image does not have an appropriate text alternative

Location

DOM selector: .center-block.img-responsive.height_full | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<img src="https://www.police.gov.bd/storage/upload/file/N2K44DzaRjd7keWG5OOpWB6ZrIhVue1E5IyKhoOB.jpg" class=" height_full img-responsive center-block" style="cursor: pointer;">

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have an alt attribute
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute
  Element's default semantics were not overridden with role="none" or role="presentation"

axe description

Ensure <img> elements have alternative text or a role of none or presentation

Determine whether the image is informative, functional, or decorative. Informative images should have concise alternative text describing their purpose. Decorative images should normally use alt="".

<img alt="[Describe the image purpose]" class="height_full img-responsive center-block" src="https://www.police.gov.bd/storage/upload/file/N2K44DzaRjd7keWG5OOpWB6ZrIhVue1E5IyKhoOB.jpg" style="cursor: pointer;"/>

#050

Link does not have a discernible accessible name

link-name  •  UF-00050
High axe Links WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value Level A Axe automated finding
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Screen-reader users may encounter a link without being told what it does or where it goes.

Location

DOM selector: .z-index-300 > a[target="_blank"] | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<a href="https://webmail.police.gov.bd/owa" target="_blank"><i class="fa fa-envelope-o"></i> </a>

axe automated evidence 

Fix all of the following:
  Element is in tab order and does not have accessible text

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have text that is visible to screen readers
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute

axe description

Ensure links have discernible text

Recommended change

Provide meaningful visible link text or another valid accessible name. Icon-only links should expose a concise accessible name describing their action or destination.

Suggested code pattern 

<a aria-label="Describe link destination" href="https://webmail.police.gov.bd/owa" target="_blank"><i class="fa fa-envelope-o"></i> </a>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Verify the final computed accessible name in the rendered browser accessibility tree.

Reference

Fix all of the following:
  Element is in tab order and does not have accessible text

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have text that is visible to screen readers
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute

axe description

Ensure links have discernible text

Recommended change

Provide meaningful visible link text or another valid accessible name. Icon-only links should expose a concise accessible name describing their action or destination.

Suggested code pattern 

<a aria-label="Describe link destination" class="facebook_icon" href="https://www.facebook.com/BangladeshPoliceOfficialPage" target="_blank"> </a>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Verify the final computed accessible name in the rendered browser accessibility tree.

Page restricts zooming or scaling

Medium axe Visual accessibility WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text Level AA Axe automated finding

DOM selector: meta[name="viewport"] | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1">

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  maximum-scale on <meta> tag disables zooming on mobile devices

axe description

Ensure <meta name="viewport"> does not disable text scaling and zooming

Recommended change

Remove restrictions such as user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1. Allow users to zoom the page.

#184

Text color contrast requires review

color-contrast  •  UF-00184
Review axe — manual review Color contrast WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) Level AA Manual review required
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Insufficient contrast between text and its background can make content difficult to read for users with low vision or color-vision deficiencies.

Location

DOM selector: .dropdown:nth-child(1) > a[href$="www.police.gov.bd"] | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<a href="https://www.police.gov.bd"> 
                                            Home
                                                                                    </a>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element's background color could not be determined due to a background gradient

axe description

Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

Recommended change

Check the computed foreground and background colors of the affected text. Normal-sized text should generally have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, while qualifying large text should generally have a ratio of at least 3:1.

Manual review

Required: Yes

axe returned this finding as incomplete when contrast could not be conclusively evaluated automatically. Background images, gradients, transparency, overlapping elements, or other rendered styling can require manual inspection.

Reference

Open axe rule documentation

Methodology note: Automated accessibility testing can identify many important problems, but it cannot establish complete WCAG conformance. Context-dependent and incomplete findings require human review. Context-aware recommendations are produced by deterministic rules using extracted local page context and should be verified before implementation.
